verses.1:1: Now after the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.
verses.1:2: And Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and became sick; so he sent messengers and said to them, "Go, inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this sickness."
verses.1:3: But the angel of the LORD spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and speak to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron?
verses.1:4: Therefore thus says the LORD: From the bed to which you have gone up, you shall not come down, for you shall surely die.'" So Elijah departed.
verses.1:5: Then the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, "Why is it that you have returned?"
verses.1:6: And they said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him, Thus says the LORD: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore, from the bed to which you have gone up, you shall not come down, for you shall surely die.'"
verses.1:7: Then he spoke to them, "What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
verses.1:8: So they answered him, "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded about his waist." And he said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."
verses.1:9: Then he sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men. And he went up to him, and behold, he was sitting on the top of the mountain. And he spoke to him, "Man of God, the king has spoken: Come down!"
verses.1:10: And Elijah answered and spoke to the captain of the fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men." And fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
verses.1:11: Again he sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty men. And he spoke up and said to him, "Man of God, thus says the king: Come down quickly!"
verses.1:12: And Elijah answered and spoke to them, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men." Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
verses.1:13: Again he sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty men. And the third captain of fifty went up and came and bowed down upon his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, and spoke to him, "Man of God, please let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.
verses.1:14: Behold, fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two captains of fifty with their fifties; but now let my life be precious in your sight."
verses.1:15: Then the angel of the LORD spoke to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So he arose and went down with him to the king.
verses.1:16: And he spoke to him, "Thus says the LORD: Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of His word?—therefore, from the bed to which you have gone up, you shall not come down, for you shall surely die."
verses.1:17: So he died according to the word of the LORD which Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram reigned in his place in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, because he had no son.
verses.1:18: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2:1: And it came to pass, when the LORD was about to take Elijah up into heaven by a whirlwind, that Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.
verses.2:2: Then Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.
verses.2:3: And the sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is taking away your master from over your head?" And he said, "I also know it; keep silent."
verses.2:4: Then Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho." And he said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.
verses.2:5: And the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is taking away your master from over your head?" And he answered, "I also know it; keep silent."
verses.2:6: Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." And he said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.
verses.2:7: And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
verses.2:8: Now Elijah took his mantle, rolled it up, and struck the waters; and they were divided this way and that, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
verses.2:9: And it came to pass, when they had crossed over, that Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I may do for you, before I am taken away from you." And Elisha said, "Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me."
verses.2:10: So he said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be so."
verses.2:11: And it came to pass, as they walked on and talked, that behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them; and Elijah ascended by a whirlwind into heaven.
verses.2:12: And Elisha watched and cried out, "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!" And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own garments and tore them into two pieces.
verses.2:13: He also lifted up the mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him, and returned and stood by the bank of the Jordan.
verses.2:14: Then he took the mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters, and said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" And when he also had struck the waters, they were divided this way and that, and Elisha crossed over.
verses.2:15: And when the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him opposite them, they said, "The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.
verses.2:16: Then they said to him, "Behold now, there are with your servants fifty valiant men; please let them go and search for your master, lest the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up and cast him upon one of the mountains or into one of the valleys." And he said, "You shall not send them."
verses.2:17: Yet they urged him until he was ashamed, so he said, "Send them." Therefore they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days, but did not find him.
verses.2:18: And when they returned to him, while he was staying at Jericho, he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"
verses.2:19: Then the men of the city said to Elisha, "Behold now, the site of the city is good, as my lord sees; but the waters are bad, and the land is barren."
verses.2:20: And he said, "Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.
verses.2:21: Then he went out to the spring of the waters and cast salt there, and said, "Thus says the LORD: I have healed these waters; from them there shall be no more death or barrenness."
verses.2:22: So the waters were healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.
verses.2:23: Then he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up along the way, young lads came out from the city and mocked him, and said to him, "Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!"
verses.2:24: So he turned behind him and saw them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. And two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the youths.
verses.2:25: Then he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
verses.3:1: Now Jehoram the son of Ahab became king over Israel at Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
verses.3:2: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, though not like his father and his mother; for he removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.
verses.3:3: Nevertheless he clung to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin; he did not depart from them.
verses.3:4: Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheepbreeder, and he regularly paid the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
verses.3:5: But it came to pass, when Ahab died, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
verses.3:6: So King Jehoram went out of Samaria on that day and mustered all Israel.
verses.3:7: Then he went and sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab to battle?" And he said, "I will go up; I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
verses.3:8: And he said, "Which way shall we go up?" And he answered, "By way of the Wilderness of Edom."
verses.3:9: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went, and made a circuit of a seven days' journey; and there was no water for the camp nor for the beasts that followed them.
verses.3:10: And the king of Israel said, "Alas! For the LORD has called these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab."
verses.3:11: But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of the LORD through him?" Then one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, "Elisha the son of Shaphat is here, who poured water upon the hands of Elijah."
verses.3:12: And Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with him." So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.
verses.3:13: Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother." But the king of Israel said to him, "No, for the LORD has called these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab."
verses.3:14: And Elisha said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, surely were it not that I have regard for the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look toward you nor see you.
verses.3:15: But now bring me a musician." And it came to pass, as the musician played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him.
verses.3:16: And he said, "Thus says the LORD: Make this valley full of trenches.
verses.3:17: For thus says the LORD: You shall not see wind, nor shall you see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, so that you, your livestock, and your beasts shall drink.
verses.3:18: And this is a light thing in the sight of the LORD; He will also deliver Moab into your hand.
verses.3:19: And you shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and you shall fell every good tree, and stop up every spring of water, and mar every good plot of land with stones."
verses.3:20: Now it came to pass in the morning, when the grain offering was offered, that behold, water came by way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
verses.3:21: Now all Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them; and all who were able to gird on armor and older were summoned, and they stood at the border.
verses.3:22: And they rose early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the water; and the Moabites saw the water opposite them as red as blood.
verses.3:23: And they said, "This is blood! The kings have surely destroyed one another, and each man has struck down his neighbor. Now therefore, Moab, to the spoil!"
verses.3:24: So when they came to the camp of Israel, Israel rose up and struck the Moabites, so that they fled before them; and they struck into the land, even striking down Moab.
verses.3:25: And they tore down the cities, and upon every good plot of land each man cast his stone and filled it; and they stopped up every spring of water and felled every good tree, until only its stones were left in Kir Haraseth. And the slingers surrounded it and struck it.
verses.3:26: And when the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword, to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.
verses.3:27: Then he took his eldest son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel; so they departed from him and returned to their own land.
verses.4:1: Now a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD; and the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
verses.4:2: So Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a flask of oil."
verses.4:3: Then he said, "Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors—empty vessels; do not gather just a few.
verses.4:4: And you shall go in and shut the door behind yourself and behind your sons, and pour into all these vessels, and set aside each one that is full."
verses.4:5: So she departed from him and shut the door behind herself and behind her sons; they kept bringing the vessels to her, and she kept pouring out.
verses.4:6: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." And he said to her, "There is not another vessel." Then the oil ceased.
verses.4:7: Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt; and you and your sons shall live on the rest."
verses.4:8: Now it came to pass one day that Elisha crossed over to Shunem, where there was a prominent woman, and she pressed him to eat bread. And so it was, as often as he passed by, he would turn aside there to eat bread.
verses.4:9: And she said to her husband, "Behold, now I know that he is a holy man of God who passes by us continually.
verses.4:10: Let us make, please, a small walled upper chamber, and let us place there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand; and it shall be, whenever he comes to us, that he may turn aside there."
verses.4:11: And it came to pass one day that he came there, and he turned aside into the upper chamber and lay down there.
verses.4:12: Then he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." So he called her, and she stood before him.
verses.4:13: And he said to him, "Say now to her, 'Behold, you have shown all this earnest care for us. What is to be done for you? Would you have a word spoken for you to the king or to the commander of the army?'" And she answered, "I dwell in the midst of my own people."
verses.4:14: So he said, "What then is to be done for her?" And Gehazi answered, "Indeed, she has no son, and her husband is old."
verses.4:15: And he said, "Call her." When he had called her, she stood in the doorway.
verses.4:16: Then he said, "At this appointed season, about this time next year, you shall embrace a son." And she said, "No, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your maidservant!"
verses.4:17: And the woman conceived and bore a son at that appointed season, about that time the next year, just as Elisha had spoken to her.
verses.4:18: Now the child grew. And it came to pass one day that he went out to his father, to the reapers.
verses.4:19: And he said to his father, "My head, my head!" So he said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."
verses.4:20: When he had carried him and brought him to his mother, he sat on her knees until noon, and then died.
verses.4:21: And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.
verses.4:22: Then she called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, that I may run to the man of God and return."
verses.4:23: And he said, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither the New Moon nor the Sabbath." And she said, "It is well."
verses.4:24: Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on and go forward; do not slacken the pace for me unless I tell you."
verses.4:25: So she departed and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her from afar, that he said to his servant Gehazi, "Behold, there is that Shunammite woman!
verses.4:26: Please run now to meet her, and say to her, 'Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?'" And she answered, "It is well."
verses.4:27: Now when she came to the man of God at the mountain, she caught hold of his feet; and Gehazi drew near to push her away. But the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for her soul is in bitter distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me."
verses.4:28: Then she said, "Did I ask a son of my lord? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"
verses.4:29: Then he said to Gehazi, "Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him; and if anyone greets you, do not answer him; and lay my staff upon the face of the boy."
verses.4:30: And the mother of the boy said, "As the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So he arose and followed her.
verses.4:31: Now Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff upon the face of the boy, but there was neither voice nor response. Therefore he returned to meet him and told him, saying, "The boy has not awakened."
verses.4:32: When Elisha came into the house, behold, the boy was dead, laid upon his bed.
verses.4:33: So he went in, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
verses.4:34: And he went up and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and he stretched himself out upon him, and the flesh of the child grew warm.
verses.4:35: Then he returned and walked back and forth in the house, once this way and once that way, and went up and stretched himself out upon him; and the boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.
verses.4:36: And he called Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite woman." So he called her. And when she came in to him, he said, "Take up your son."
verses.4:37: So she went in, fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground; then she took up her son and went out.
verses.4:38: And Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. Now the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, and he said to his servant, "Set on the large pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."
verses.4:39: So one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered from it his garment full of wild gourds, and came and sliced them into the pot of stew, for they did not know what they were.
verses.4:40: Then they poured it out for the men to eat. Now it came to pass, as they were eating of the stew, that they cried out and said, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.
verses.4:41: So he said, "Then bring some flour." And he cast it into the pot, and said, "Pour it out for the people, that they may eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
verses.4:42: Now a man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley bread, and fresh ears of grain in his sack. And he said, "Give it to the people, that they may eat."
verses.4:43: But his attendant said, "What, shall I set this before a hundred men?" He said again, "Give it to the people, that they may eat; for thus says the LORD, 'They shall eat and have some left over.'"
verses.4:44: So he set it before them; and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the LORD.
verses.5:1: Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his master and held in high honor, because by him the LORD had given deliverance to Aram. And the man was a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.
verses.5:2: Now the Arameans had gone out in raiding bands, and had carried away captive a little girl from the land of Israel; and she waited on Naaman's wife.
verses.5:3: And she said to her mistress, "If only my master were before the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy."
verses.5:4: And he went in and told his master, saying, "Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from the land of Israel."
verses.5:5: Then the king of Aram said, "Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he departed and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten changes of garments.
verses.5:6: And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, which said, "Now, when this letter comes to you, behold, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, that you may heal him of his leprosy."
verses.5:7: And it came to pass, when the king of Israel read the letter, that he tore his garments and said, "Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends word to me to heal a man of his leprosy? Therefore, please consider and see how he is seeking a quarrel against me!"
verses.5:8: So it was, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his garments, that he sent to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your garments? Let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel."
verses.5:9: Then Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the doorway of the house of Elisha.
verses.5:10: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall be restored to you, and you shall be clean."
verses.5:11: But Naaman became furious and went away, and said, "Behold, I said to myself, 'He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call upon the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the place, and cure the leper.'
verses.5:12: Are not Amanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and departed in wrath.
verses.5:13: And his servants drew near and spoke to him, and said, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more then, when he says to you, 'Wash, and be clean'?"
verses.5:14: So he went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
verses.5:15: And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came and stood before him; and he said, "Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel; now therefore, please accept a gift from your servant."
verses.5:16: But he said, "As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will receive nothing." And he urged him to take it, but he refused.
verses.5:17: Then Naaman said, "If not, please let your servant be given two mules' load of earth; for your servant will no longer offer either burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the LORD.
verses.5:18: Yet in this matter may the LORD pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon—when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD pardon your servant in this matter."
verses.5:19: Then he said to him, "Go in peace." So he departed from him a short distance.
verses.5:20: But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, "Behold, my master has spared Naaman this Aramean, in not receiving from his hand what he brought; but as the LORD lives, I will surely run after him and take something from him."
verses.5:21: So Gehazi pursued Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running after him, he stepped down from the chariot to meet him, and said, "Is all well?"
verses.5:22: And he said, "All is well. My master has sent me, saying, 'Behold, just now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of garments.'"
verses.5:23: So Naaman said, "Be pleased to take two talents." And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and gave them to two of his servants; and they carried them before him.
verses.5:24: And when he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and stored them away in the house; then he let the men go, and they departed.
verses.5:25: Now he went in and stood before his master. And Elisha said to him, "Where have you come from, Gehazi?" And he said, "Your servant did not go anywhere."
verses.5:26: Then he said to him, "Did not my heart go with you when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to receive silver and to receive garments, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen, male servants and maidservants?
verses.5:27: Therefore the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your descendants forever." And he went out from his presence leprous, as white as snow.
verses.6:1: Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Behold now, the place where we dwell before you is too narrow for us.
verses.6:2: Let us go, please, to the Jordan, and let every man take one beam from there, and let us make a place there for ourselves to dwell." And he said, "Go."
verses.6:3: Then one of them said, "Please consent and go with your servants." And he said, "I will go."
verses.6:4: So he went with them; and they came to the Jordan and cut down trees.
verses.6:5: And it came to pass, as one was felling a beam, that the iron fell into the water; and he cried out and said, "Alas, my master! For it was borrowed!"
verses.6:6: Then the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place. So he cut off a stick, cast it in there, and made the iron float.
verses.6:7: And he said, "Lift it up for yourself." So he reached out his hand and took it.
verses.6:8: Now the king of Syria was warring against Israel; and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "In such and such a place shall be my encampment."
verses.6:9: And the man of God sent word to the king of Israel, saying, "Take heed that you do not pass by this place, for the Syrians are coming down there."
verses.6:10: Then the king of Israel sent to the place of which the man of God had spoken to him and warned him, and he guarded himself there, not once and not twice.
verses.6:11: Therefore the heart of the king of Syria was greatly agitated over this matter; and he summoned his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me which of our own is for the king of Israel?"
verses.6:12: And one of his servants said, "None, my lord, O king; rather, Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the very words that you speak in your bedchamber."
verses.6:13: So he said, "Go and see where he is, that I may send and seize him." And it was told him, saying, "Behold, he is in Dothan."
verses.6:14: Therefore he sent horses and chariots and a mighty force there, and they came by night and surrounded the city.
verses.6:15: Now when the attendant of the man of God rose early and went out, behold, a host was encircling the city with horses and chariots. And his servant said to him, "Alas, my master! What shall we do?"
verses.6:16: And he answered, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
verses.6:17: Then Elisha prayed and said, "O LORD, please open his eyes that he may see." And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he looked; and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
verses.6:18: And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, "Please strike this people with blindness." And He struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
verses.6:19: Then Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, nor is this the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man whom you seek." So he led them to Samaria.
verses.6:20: And it came to pass, when they had entered Samaria, that Elisha said, "O LORD, open the eyes of these men, that they may see." And the LORD opened their eyes, and they looked; and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
verses.6:21: Now when the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them? Shall I strike them?"
verses.6:22: And he answered, "You shall not strike them. Would you strike down those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink and go to their master."
verses.6:23: So he prepared a great feast for them; and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the raiding bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel.
verses.6:24: And it came to pass after this that Ben-Hadad king of Syria gathered all his army, and went up and besieged Samaria.
verses.6:25: And there was a great famine in Samaria; and behold, they besieged it until a donkey's head was sold for eighty pieces of silver, and one-fourth of a kab of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.
verses.6:26: Then, as the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, saying, "Help, my lord, O king!"
verses.6:27: And he said, "If the LORD does not help you, from where shall I help you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?"
verses.6:28: Then the king said to her, "What troubles you?" And she answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'
verses.6:29: So we boiled my son and ate him. And I said to her on the next day, 'Give your son, that we may eat him'; but she has hidden her son."
verses.6:30: Now it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he tore his garments; and as he passed by on the wall, the people looked, and behold, underneath he had sackcloth upon his flesh.
verses.6:31: Then he said, "May God do so to me and more also, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat remains on him this day!"
verses.6:32: Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And the king sent a man from before him; yet before the messenger came to him, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to take off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold him fast at the door. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
verses.6:33: While he was still speaking with them, behold, the messenger came down to him; and he said, "Behold, this calamity is from the LORD! Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"
verses.7:1: Then Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD! Thus says the LORD: 'Tomorrow about this time a seah of fine flour shall be sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.'"
verses.7:2: Then the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God and said, "Behold, even if the LORD should make windows in heaven, could this thing be?" And he said, "Behold, you shall see it with your own eyes, yet you shall not eat of it."
verses.7:3: Now there were four leprous men at the entrance of the gate; and they said to one another, "Why are we sitting here until we die?
verses.7:4: If we say, 'We will enter the city,' the famine is in the city, and we shall die there. And if we sit here, we die also. Now therefore, come, let us surrender to the camp of the Syrians. If they keep us alive, we shall live; and if they put us to death, we shall die."
verses.7:5: And they arose at twilight to go to the camp of the Syrians; and when they came to the outskirts of the camp of the Syrians, behold, there was no one there.
verses.7:6: For the Lord had caused the camp of the Syrians to hear the sound of chariots and the sound of horses, the sound of a great army; so they said to one another, "Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come upon us!"
verses.7:7: Therefore they arose and fled at twilight, and abandoned their tents, their horses, and their donkeys—the camp just as it was—and fled for their lives.
verses.7:8: And when these lepers came to the outskirts of the camp, they went into one tent and ate and drank, and carried away from it silver and gold and garments, and went and hid them. Then they returned and entered another tent, and carried things away from there also, and went and hid them.
verses.7:9: Then they said to one another, "We are not doing right. This day is a day of good tidings, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until the light of morning, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore, come, let us go and tell the household of the king."
verses.7:10: So they went and called to the gatekeepers of the city, and told them, saying, "We came to the camp of the Syrians, and behold, there is no one there, nor the voice of any man, only horses tied and donkeys tied, and the tents just as they were."
verses.7:11: And the gatekeepers called out, and they reported it to the king's household within.
verses.7:12: So the king arose in the night and said to his servants, "Let me now tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are hungry; therefore they have gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, 'When they come out of the city, we shall seize them alive and enter the city.'"
verses.7:13: And one of his servants answered and said, "Please let men take five of the remaining horses that are left in the city—behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are left in it; behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel who have perished—and let us send and see."
verses.7:14: So they took two chariots with horses; and the king sent them after the army of the Syrians, saying, "Go and see."
verses.7:15: And they went after them to the Jordan; and behold, all the road was full of garments and equipment which the Syrians had cast away in their haste. So the messengers returned and told the king.
verses.7:16: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Syrians. So a seah of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.
verses.7:17: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned to have charge of the gate; and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken, who spoke when the king came down to him.
verses.7:18: So it came to pass just as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, "Two seahs of barley for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, shall be sold tomorrow about this time in the gate of Samaria."
verses.7:19: And that officer had answered the man of God and said, "Now behold, even if the LORD should make windows in heaven, could such a thing as this be?" And he had said, "Behold, you shall see it with your own eyes, yet you shall not eat of it."
verses.7:20: And so it happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.
verses.8:1: Now Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, "Arise and depart, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you can sojourn; for the LORD has called for a famine, and it shall indeed come upon the land for seven years."
verses.8:2: So the woman arose and did according to the word of the man of God; and she went, she and her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.
verses.8:3: And it came to pass at the end of seven years that the woman returned from the land of the Philistines; and she went out to cry out to the king concerning her house and her field.
verses.8:4: Now the king was speaking to Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, "Please tell me all the great deeds that Elisha has done."
verses.8:5: And it happened, as he was telling the king how he had restored the dead to life, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life was crying out to the king for her house and for her field. And Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life."
verses.8:6: And when the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed a certain officer for her, saying, "Restore all that belonged to her, and all the produce of the field from the day that she left the land until now."
verses.8:7: Then Elisha came to Damascus, and Ben-Hadad king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, "The man of God has come here."
verses.8:8: And the king said to Hazael, "Take a present in your hand, and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the LORD by him, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"
verses.8:9: So Hazael went to meet him and took a present in his hand, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camel-loads; and he came and stood before him, and said, "Your son Ben-Hadad king of Syria has sent me to you, saying, 'Shall I recover from this sickness?'"
verses.8:10: And Elisha said to him, "Go, say to him, 'You shall surely recover.' Yet the LORD has shown me that he shall surely die."
verses.8:11: Then he fixed his countenance and stared until he was ashamed; and the man of God wept.
verses.8:12: And Hazael said, "Why does my lord weep?" And he answered, "Because I know the evil that you will do to the children of Israel: their strongholds you shall set on fire, and their young men you shall slay with the sword, and their little ones you shall dash in pieces, and their women with child you shall rip open."
verses.8:13: Then Hazael said, "But what is your servant, who is but a dog, that he should do this great thing?" And Elisha answered, "The LORD has shown me that you shall be king over Syria."
verses.8:14: So he departed from Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he answered, "He said to me, 'You shall surely recover.'"
verses.8:15: And it came to pass on the next day that he took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over his face, so that he died. And Hazael reigned in his place.
verses.8:16: Now in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.8:17: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.8:18: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.8:19: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David His servant, as He had promised him to give him a lamp for his sons always.
verses.8:20: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and set a king over themselves.
verses.8:21: So Joram crossed over to Zair, and all the chariots with him. Then he arose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the captains of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents.
verses.8:22: Thus Edom has been in revolt from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah also revolted at that same time.
verses.8:23: Now the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.8:24: So Joram rested with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Then Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.8:25: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.8:26: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
verses.8:27: And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
verses.8:28: Now he went with Joram the son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram.
verses.8:29: Then King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds which the Syrians had inflicted on him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
verses.9:1: And Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets, and said to him, "Gird up your loins, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.9:2: When you arrive there, look out there for Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi, and go in and make him rise up from among his brethren, and bring him into an inner chamber.
verses.9:3: Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head, and say, 'Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee, and do not delay."
verses.9:4: So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.9:5: And when he arrived, behold, the captains of the army were sitting there; and he said, "I have a message for you, O captain." And Jehu said, "For which one of us all?" And he said, "For you, O captain."
verses.9:6: Then he arose and went into the house. And he poured the oil on his head, and said to him, "Thus says the LORD God of Israel: 'I have anointed you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.
verses.9:7: You shall strike down the house of Ahab your master, that I may avenge the blood of My servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the LORD, at the hand of Jezebel.
verses.9:8: For the whole house of Ahab shall perish; and I will cut off from Ahab every male, both bond and free, in Israel.
verses.9:9: And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.
verses.9:10: The dogs shall eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her.'" And he opened the door and fled.
verses.9:11: Then Jehu came out to the servants of his master, and one said to him, "Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?" And he said to them, "You know the man and his talk."
verses.9:12: And they said, "That is false! Tell us now." So he said, "Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.'"
verses.9:13: Then each man hastened and took his garment and placed it under him on the bare steps; and they blew the trumpet and cried out, "Jehu is king!"
verses.9:14: So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been defending Ramoth Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria.
verses.9:15: But King Jehoram had returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds which the Syrians had inflicted on him, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Jehu said, "If this is your mind, let no fugitive escape from the city to go and report it in Jezreel."
verses.9:16: So Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram was laid up there; and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see Joram.
verses.9:17: Now a watchman stood on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw the company of Jehu as he came, and said, "I see a company." And Jehoram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"
verses.9:18: So the horseman went to meet him, and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me." So the watchman reported, saying, "The messenger reached them, but he has not returned."
verses.9:19: Then he sent out a second horseman, who came to them and said, "Thus says the king: 'Peace?'" And Jehu answered, "What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me."
verses.9:20: So the watchman reported, saying, "He reached them and has not returned; and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously."
verses.9:21: Then Jehoram said, "Make ready!" And his chariot was made ready. So Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot; and they went out to meet Jehu, and found him on the plot of ground of Naboth the Jezreelite.
verses.9:22: Now it came to pass, when Jehoram saw Jehu, that he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And he answered, "What peace can there be, so long as the harlotries of your mother Jezebel and her witchcrafts are so many?"
verses.9:23: Then Jehoram turned about and fled, and said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
verses.9:24: Now Jehu drew his bow with full strength and shot Jehoram between his shoulders; and the arrow went out through his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.
verses.9:25: Then Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up, and cast him into the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember how you and I were riding together behind Ahab his father, when the LORD laid this burden upon him:
verses.9:26: 'Surely I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons,' says the LORD, 'and I will repay you in this very plot,' says the LORD. Now therefore, pick him up and cast him into the plot, according to the word of the LORD."
verses.9:27: And when Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled by the road to Beth Haggan. So Jehu pursued him and said, "Strike him also in the chariot," at the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam. Then he fled to Megiddo, and died there.
verses.9:28: And his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the City of David.
verses.9:29: Now in the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab, Ahaziah had begun to reign over Judah.
verses.9:30: Now when Jehu had come to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; and she painted her eyes and adorned her head, and looked out through a window.
verses.9:31: Then, as Jehu entered at the gate, she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
verses.9:32: And he lifted up his face toward the window, and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" And two or three eunuchs looked out at him.
verses.9:33: Then he said, "Throw her down!" So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses; and he trampled her underfoot.
verses.9:34: And when he had gone in, he ate and drank. Then he said, "Go, see now to this accursed woman and bury her, for she was a king's daughter."
verses.9:35: So they went to bury her, but they found no more of her than the skull and the feet and the palms of her hands.
verses.9:36: Therefore they came back and told him. And he said, "This is the word of the LORD, which He spoke by His servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, 'In the territory of Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel;
verses.9:37: and the corpse of Jezebel shall be as refuse on the surface of the field in the territory of Jezreel, so that they shall not say, "This is Jezebel."'"
verses.10:1: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab's sons, saying,
verses.10:2: "Now, as soon as this letter reaches you, since your master's sons are with you, and with you are chariots and horses, a fortified city also, and weapons,
verses.10:3: select the best and most upright of your master's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house."
verses.10:4: But they feared exceedingly and said, "Behold, the two kings did not stand before him; how then shall we stand?"
verses.10:5: So he who was over the palace, and he who was over the city, together with the elders and the guardians, sent to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, and all that you say to us we will do. We will not make any man king; do what is good in your sight."
verses.10:6: Then he wrote them a letter a second time, saying, "If you are for me, and if you listen to my voice, take the heads of the men who are your master's sons, and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, who were rearing them.
verses.10:7: And it came to pass, when the letter reached them, that they took the king's sons and slaughtered seventy men, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezreel.
verses.10:8: Then a messenger came and told him, saying, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." And he said, "Lay them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
verses.10:9: And it came to pass in the morning that he went out and stood, and said to all the people, "You are righteous. Behold, I conspired against my master and slew him; yet who struck down all these?
verses.10:10: Know now that nothing of the word of the LORD shall fall to the earth, which the LORD spoke concerning the house of Ahab; for the LORD has performed what He spoke by the hand of His servant Elijah."
verses.10:11: So Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, his close companions, and his priests, until he left him no survivor.
verses.10:12: Then he arose and departed, and went to Samaria; along the way he was at Beth Eked of the Shepherds.
verses.10:13: And Jehu met the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah, and said, "Who are you?" And they answered, "We are the brethren of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."
verses.10:14: So he said, "Seize them alive!" And they seized them alive, and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth Eked, forty-two men; and he did not leave a single man of them.
verses.10:15: When he departed from there, he met Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him; and he greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart upright, as my heart is with your heart?" And Jehonadab answered, "It is." And Jehu said, "If it is, give me your hand." So he gave him his hand, and he brought him up to himself into the chariot.
verses.10:16: Then he said, "Come with me, and see my zeal for the LORD." So they had him ride in his chariot.
verses.10:17: And when he came to Samaria, he struck down all who remained to Ahab in Samaria until he had destroyed him, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke to Elijah.
verses.10:18: Then Jehu gathered all the people together and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little, but Jehu will serve him much.
verses.10:19: Now therefore, summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers, and all his priests. Let no man be missing, for I have a great sacrifice for Baal; whoever is missing shall not live." Yet Jehu acted with subtlety, in order to destroy the worshipers of Baal.
verses.10:20: And Jehu said, "Consecrate a solemn assembly for Baal." So they proclaimed it.
verses.10:21: Then Jehu sent throughout all Israel; and all the worshipers of Baal came, so that not a man remained who did not come. And they entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from one end to the other.
verses.10:22: And he said to the one in charge of the wardrobe, "Bring out vestments for all the worshipers of Baal." So he brought out the vestments for them.
verses.10:23: Then Jehu and Jehonadab the son of Rechab entered the house of Baal, and he said to the worshipers of Baal, "Search and see lest there be here with you any of the servants of the LORD, rather than the worshipers of Baal alone."
verses.10:24: So they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside for himself, and he said, "Whoever lets any of the men escape whom I bring into your hands, his own life shall be in place of his life."
verses.10:25: And it came to pass, as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the guards and to the officers, "Go in and strike them down; let no man come out!" So they struck them down with the edge of the sword; and the guards and the officers cast them out, and went into the inner sanctuary of the house of Baal.
verses.10:26: And they brought out the sacred pillars of the house of Baal and burned them.
verses.10:27: They also broke down the sacred pillar of Baal, and tore down the house of Baal and turned it into a latrine to this day.
verses.10:28: Thus Jehu eradicated Baal from Israel.
verses.10:29: However, Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he had made Israel sin—that is, the golden calves that were at Bethel and at Dan.
verses.10:30: And the LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in My sight, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in My heart, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel."
verses.10:31: Yet Jehu did not take heed to walk in the law of the LORD God of Israel with all his heart; he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, with which he had made Israel sin.
verses.10:32: In those days the LORD began to cut off parts of Israel; and Hazael struck them throughout all the territory of Israel:
verses.10:33: from the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, all the land of Gilead—the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites—from Aroer, which is by the Brook Arnon, including Gilead and Bashan.
verses.10:34: Now the rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.10:35: So Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. Then Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:36: And the period that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years.
verses.11:1: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring.
verses.11:2: But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death, placing him and his nurse in the bedchamber. Thus they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not put to death.
verses.11:3: And he remained hidden with her in the house of the LORD six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.11:4: In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and brought the captains of hundreds of the Carites and of the guards, and brought them to himself into the house of the LORD. And he made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD, and showed them the king's son.
verses.11:5: Then he commanded them, saying, "This is the thing that you shall do: one-third of you who come on duty on the Sabbath shall keep the watch of the king's house,
verses.11:6: one-third shall be at the Gate of Sur, and one-third at the gate behind the guards; thus you shall keep the watch of the house as a defense.
verses.11:7: And the two divisions of you, all who go off duty on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the LORD around the king.
verses.11:8: And you shall surround the king on every side, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whoever approaches the ranks shall be put to death. You shall be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."
verses.11:9: So the captains of hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each of them took his men who were coming on duty on the Sabbath, together with those who were going off duty on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.11:10: And the priest gave the captains of hundreds the spears and shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of the LORD.
verses.11:11: Then the guards stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, beside the altar and the house, all around the king.
verses.11:12: And he brought out the king's son, put the crown upon him, and gave him the Testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, "Long live the king!"
verses.11:13: Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she came to the people in the house of the LORD.
verses.11:14: And she looked, and behold, the king stood by the pillar according to custom; and the captains and the trumpeters were beside the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her garments and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"
verses.11:15: And Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and slay with the sword whoever follows her." For the priest had said, "Do not let her be put to death in the house of the LORD."
verses.11:16: So they laid hands on her; and she went by way of the horses' entrance into the king's house, and there she was put to death.
verses.11:17: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people, that they should be the LORD's people, and also between the king and the people.
verses.11:18: And all the people of the land went to the house of Baal and tore it down; they shattered its altars and its images thoroughly, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed officers over the house of the LORD.
verses.11:19: Then he took the captains of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land; and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD, and came by way of the Gate of the Guards to the king's house. And he sat on the throne of the kings.
verses.11:20: So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; for they had slain Athaliah with the sword at the king's house.
verses.12:1: Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign.
verses.12:2: In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
verses.12:3: And Jehoash did what was right in the sight of the LORD all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
verses.12:4: Yet the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
verses.12:5: And Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money of the consecrated offerings that is brought into the house of the LORD—the assessment money for each man, the money for each person's valuation, and all the money that comes into a man's heart to bring into the house of the LORD—
verses.12:6: let the priests receive it for themselves, each from his acquaintance, and let them repair the breaches of the house, wherever any breach is found."
verses.12:7: Now it came to pass, in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, that the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house.
verses.12:8: So King Jehoash called Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the breaches of the house? Now therefore, do not take money from your acquaintances, but give it for the breaches of the house."
verses.12:9: And the priests consented neither to receive money from the people nor to repair the breaches of the house.
verses.12:10: Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD; and the priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.
verses.12:11: And it came to pass, whenever they saw that there was much money in the chest, that the king's scribe and the high priest went up, put it in bags, and counted the money that was found in the house of the LORD.
verses.12:12: Then they gave the money that had been weighed out into the hands of those who did the work, who had the oversight of the house of the LORD; and they paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the house of the LORD,
verses.12:13: and to the masons and stonecutters, and for buying timber and hewn stone to repair the breaches of the house of the LORD, and for all that was spent on the house to repair it.
verses.12:14: However, there were not made for the house of the LORD silver basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any vessels of gold or silver from the money brought into the house of the LORD.
verses.12:15: For they gave it to those who did the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
verses.12:16: Moreover, they did not ask for an accounting from the men into whose hands they delivered the money to pay the workmen, for they dealt faithfully.
verses.12:17: The money from trespass offerings and the money from sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.
verses.12:18: At that time Hazael king of Syria went up, fought against Gath, and captured it; then Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
verses.12:19: And Jehoash king of Judah took all the consecrated things that his fathers—Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, kings of Judah—had dedicated, along with his own consecrated things and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, and sent them to Hazael king of Syria. So he withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.12:20: Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.12:21: And his servants arose and formed a conspiracy, and struck Joash down at Beth Millo, on the way down to Silla.
verses.12:22: For Jozachar the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died. And they buried him with his fathers in the City of David, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria for seventeen years.
verses.13:2: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, and walked after the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, by which he had caused Israel to sin; he did not turn away from them.
verses.13:3: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Ben-Hadad the son of Hazael, all those days.
verses.13:4: Then Jehoahaz implored the favor of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him; for He saw the oppression of Israel, because the king of Syria oppressed them.
verses.13:5: So the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from under the hand of Syria; and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents as in former times.
verses.13:6: Nevertheless they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, by which he had caused Israel to sin, but walked in them; and the Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.
verses.13:7: For there was not left to Jehoahaz an army except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Syria had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.
verses.13:8: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:9: So Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:10: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
verses.13:11: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, by which he had caused Israel to sin, but walked in them.
verses.13:12: Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:13: So Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
verses.13:14: Now Elisha had fallen sick with the illness of which he was to die. Then Joash the king of Israel came down to him, wept over his face, and said, "My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"
verses.13:15: And Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took for himself a bow and arrows.
verses.13:16: Then he said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." So he put his hand on it, and Elisha laid his hands upon the hands of the king.
verses.13:17: And he said, "Open the window eastward." And he opened it. Then Elisha said, "Shoot!" And he shot. And he said, "The arrow of the LORD's deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance over Syria! For you shall strike down Syria at Aphek until it is wholly consumed."
verses.13:18: Then he said, "Take the arrows." So he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground!" So he struck three times and stopped.
verses.13:19: And the man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck down Syria until it was wholly consumed. But now you shall strike down Syria only three times."
verses.13:20: Then Elisha died, and they buried him. Now raiding bands of Moab used to invade the land at the coming of the year.
verses.13:21: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, behold, they saw a raiding band; and they cast the man into the tomb of Elisha. And when the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood up on his feet.
verses.13:22: Now Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
verses.13:23: But the LORD was gracious to them, had compassion on them, and turned toward them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and He would not destroy them, nor has He cast them away from His presence until now.
verses.13:24: Then Hazael king of Syria died, and Ben-Hadad his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:25: And Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took back from the hand of Ben-Hadad the son of Hazael the cities that he had taken from the hand of Jehoahaz his father in war. Three times Joash defeated him and recovered the cities of Israel.
verses.14:1: In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.14:2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
verses.14:3: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like David his father; according to all that Joash his father had done, so he did.
verses.14:4: Only the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
verses.14:5: And it came to pass, as soon as the kingdom was established firmly in his hand, that he struck down his servants who had slain the king his father.
verses.14:6: Yet he did not put to death the children of the slayers, according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, in which the LORD commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor shall children be put to death for their fathers; rather, each man shall be put to death for his own sin."
verses.14:7: He struck down ten thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt, and captured Sela in war, and called its name Joktheel to this very day.
verses.14:8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."
verses.14:9: And Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' Then a wild beast of the field that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled down the thistle.
verses.14:10: You have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Enjoy your honor and remain in your own house; for why should you provoke disaster, so that you fall—you and Judah with you?"
verses.14:11: Yet Amaziah would not listen. Therefore Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Beth Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.14:12: And Judah was defeated before Israel, and they fled, every man to his tent.
verses.14:13: Then Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh; and he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
verses.14:14: And he took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, together with hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.14:15: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
verses.14:16: So Jehoash slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
verses.14:17: And Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.14:18: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
verses.14:19: And they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; yet they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.14:20: Then they brought him back upon horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
verses.14:21: And all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.14:22: He built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.14:23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty-one years.
verses.14:24: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he had caused Israel to sin.
verses.14:25: He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, which He had spoken by the hand of His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath Hepher.
verses.14:26: For the LORD saw that the affliction of Israel was exceedingly bitter; there was neither bond nor free left, nor was there any helper for Israel.
verses.14:27: And the LORD had not said that He would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven; therefore He delivered them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.
verses.14:28: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he waged war, and how he restored to Israel Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
verses.14:29: So Jeroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel; and Zechariah his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:2: He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
verses.15:3: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
verses.15:4: Only the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
verses.15:5: And the LORD afflicted the king, so that he was a leper until the day of his death, and he dwelt in a separate house. And Jotham the king's son was over the royal household, judging the people of the land.
verses.15:6: Now the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
verses.15:7: So Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of David; and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.
verses.15:9: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his fathers had done; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he had caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:10: Then Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him down before the people and put him to death, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:11: Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
verses.15:12: This was the word of the LORD which He spoke to Jehu, saying, "Your sons to the fourth generation shall sit upon the throne of Israel." And so it came to pass.
verses.15:13: Shallum son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
verses.15:14: Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and he struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and put him to death, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:15: Now the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy which he formed, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
verses.15:16: At that time Menahem struck down Tiphsah, and all who were in it, and its territory from Tirzah onward; because it did not open to him, he struck it down, and he ripped open all its women who were with child.
verses.15:17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi began to reign over Israel, and reigned ten years in Samaria.
verses.15:18: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not depart all his days from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he had caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:19: Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hands might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.
verses.15:20: And Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from all the mighty men of wealth, fifty shekels of silver from each man, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not remain there in the land.
verses.15:21: Now the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
verses.15:22: So Menahem slept with his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned two years.
verses.15:24: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he had caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:25: Then Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the king's house, along with Argob and Arieh; and with him were fifty men of the Gileadites. Thus he put him to death and reigned in his place.
verses.15:26: Now the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
verses.15:27: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned twenty years.
verses.15:28: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he had caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:29: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee—all the land of Naphtali—and he carried them captive to Assyria.
verses.15:30: Then Hoshea son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, and struck him down and put him to death, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
verses.15:31: Now the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
verses.15:32: In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:33: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
verses.15:34: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD; according to all that Uzziah his father had done, so he did.
verses.15:35: Only the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD.
verses.15:36: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham which he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
verses.15:37: In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
verses.15:38: So Jotham slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.16:1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.16:2: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; yet he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, as David his father had done.
verses.16:3: But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel; indeed, he even made his son pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed from before the children of Israel.
verses.16:4: And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, and upon the hills, and beneath every green tree.
verses.16:5: Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem to wage war; and they besieged Ahaz, yet they could not prevail in battle.
verses.16:6: At that time Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath for Syria, and expelled the Judeans from Eloth; and the Edomites came to Elath and have dwelt there to this day.
verses.16:7: So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and deliver me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."
verses.16:8: And Ahaz took the silver and the gold that was found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasuries of the king's house, and sent it as a present to the king of Assyria.
verses.16:9: So the king of Assyria heeded him; for the king of Assyria went up against Damascus and captured it, and carried its people into exile to Kir, and put Rezin to death.
verses.16:10: Then King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria, and he saw the altar that was in Damascus; and King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its pattern, according to all its workmanship.
verses.16:11: And Uriah the priest built the altar; according to all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, so Uriah the priest made it before King Ahaz came from Damascus.
verses.16:12: And when the king came from Damascus, the king looked upon the altar; and the king drew near to the altar and went up upon it.
verses.16:13: He burned his burnt offering and his grain offering, and poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings upon the altar.
verses.16:14: And the bronze altar that stood before the LORD he moved from the front of the house, from between the altar and the house of the LORD, and set it on the north side of the altar.
