verses.16:15: Then King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "Upon the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering, and the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offering and their drink offerings; and all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice you shall sprinkle upon it. As for the bronze altar, it shall be for me to inquire by."
verses.16:16: Thus Uriah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded.
verses.16:17: And King Ahaz cut off the panels of the stands and removed the laver from them; he also took down the Sea from off the bronze oxen that were under it, and placed it upon a pavement of stones.
verses.16:18: Also the covered portico of the Sabbath that they had built in the house, and the king's outer entryway, he removed from the house of the LORD on account of the king of Assyria.
verses.16:19: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
verses.16:20: So Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of David; and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.17:1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea the son of Elah began to reign in Samaria over Israel, reigning nine years.
verses.17:2: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, yet not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.17:3: Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.
verses.17:4: But the king of Assyria uncovered a conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, and had brought up no tribute to the king of Assyria as year by year; therefore the king of Assyria confined him and bound him in prison.
verses.17:5: Then the king of Assyria marched throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria and besieged it three years.
verses.17:6: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried Israel away into exile to Assyria, and settled them in Halah and by the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
verses.17:7: Now this came to pass because the children of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from beneath the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and they had feared other gods,
verses.17:8: and walked in the statutes of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed from before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which they had instituted.
verses.17:9: And the children of Israel secretly did things that were not right against the LORD their God; and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.
verses.17:10: They set up for themselves sacred pillars and Asherah poles upon every high hill and beneath every green tree.
verses.17:11: And there they burned incense on all the high places, like the nations whom the LORD had carried away from before them; and they did evil things to provoke the LORD to anger.
verses.17:12: And they served idols, concerning which the LORD had said to them, "You shall not do this thing."
verses.17:13: Yet the LORD testified against Israel and against Judah, by the hand of all the prophets, every seer, saying, "Turn from your evil ways, and keep My commandments and My statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by the hand of My servants the prophets."
verses.17:14: Yet they would not listen, but stiffened their necks, like the neck of their fathers, who did not believe in the LORD their God.
verses.17:15: They rejected His statutes and His covenant that He had made with their fathers, and His testimonies which He had testified against them; and they went after vanity and became vain, and went after the nations that were all around them, concerning whom the LORD had commanded them that they should not do like them.
verses.17:16: So they forsook all the commandments of the LORD their God, and made for themselves molten images—two calves—and made an Asherah pole, and worshiped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
verses.17:17: And they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, and practiced divination and soothsaying, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.17:18: Therefore the LORD was exceedingly angry with Israel, and removed them from His presence; none was left except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.17:19: Judah also did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they had made.
verses.17:20: And the LORD rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of plunderers, until He had cast them out from His presence.
verses.17:21: For He tore Israel away from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king. Then Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD, and caused them to commit a great sin.
verses.17:22: And the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he committed; they did not depart from them,
verses.17:23: until the LORD removed Israel from His presence, as He had spoken by the hand of all His servants the prophets. So Israel was carried away into exile from their own land to Assyria, to this day.
verses.17:24: Then the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the children of Israel; and they took possession of Samaria and dwelt in its cities.
verses.17:25: And it came to pass, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear the LORD; therefore the LORD sent lions among them, which slew some of them.
verses.17:26: So they spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, "The nations whom you have carried into exile and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the custom of the God of the land; therefore He has sent lions among them, and behold, they are slaying them, because they do not know the custom of the God of the land."
verses.17:27: Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, "Send back there one of the priests whom you carried away from there, and let them go and dwell there; and let him teach them the custom of the God of the land."
verses.17:28: Then one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Bethel, and he taught them how they should fear the LORD.
verses.17:29: Yet every nation continued making its own gods, and placed them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities in which they dwelt.
verses.17:30: The men of Babylon made Succoth-Benoth, the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,
verses.17:31: and the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
verses.17:32: They also feared the LORD, and appointed for themselves from every class among them priests of the high places, who sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places.
verses.17:33: They feared the LORD, yet they served their own gods, according to the custom of the nations from among whom they had been carried into exile.
verses.17:34: To this day they continue doing according to the former customs: they do not fear the LORD, nor do they act according to their statutes or their ordinances, or according to the law and the commandment which the LORD commanded the children of Jacob, whom He named Israel,
verses.17:35: with whom the LORD had made a covenant and commanded them, saying, "You shall not fear other gods, nor bow down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them;
verses.17:36: but the LORD, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm, Him you shall fear, and to Him you shall bow down, and to Him you shall sacrifice.
verses.17:37: And the statutes, and the ordinances, and the law, and the commandment which He wrote for you, you shall be careful to observe always; and you shall not fear other gods.
verses.17:38: And the covenant that I have made with you, you shall not forget, neither shall you fear other gods;
verses.17:39: but the LORD your God you shall fear; and He shall deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."
verses.17:40: Yet they did not listen, but they continued doing according to their former custom.
verses.17:41: So these nations feared the LORD, yet they served their carved images; also their children and their children's children continue doing as their fathers did, to this day.
verses.18:1: Now it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.18:2: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Abi the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.18:3: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that David his father had done.
verses.18:4: He removed the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah, and crushed to pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made; for until those days the children of Israel had been burning incense to it, and he called it Nehushtan.
verses.18:5: He trusted in the LORD God of Israel, so that after him there was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among those who were before him.
verses.18:6: For he held fast to the LORD; he did not turn away from following Him, but kept His commandments, which the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.18:7: And the LORD was with him; wherever he went forth, he prospered. And he rebelled against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.
verses.18:8: He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city.
verses.18:9: Now it came to pass in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.
verses.18:10: And at the end of three years they captured it; in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
verses.18:11: Then the king of Assyria carried Israel away captive to Assyria, and settled them in Halah and by the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,
verses.18:12: because they did not obey the voice of the LORD their God, but transgressed His covenant—all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded—and they would neither listen nor do it.
verses.18:13: Now in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.
verses.18:14: Then Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, "I have done wrong; withdraw from me. Whatever you impose upon me I will bear." And the king of Assyria assessed Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.18:15: So Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house.
verses.18:16: At that time Hezekiah stripped the doors of the temple of the LORD, and the doorposts that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave them to the king of Assyria.
verses.18:17: Then the king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a great army to Jerusalem. And they went up and came to Jerusalem. When they had gone up and come, they took their stand by the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is on the highway to the Fuller's Field.
verses.18:18: And when they called to the king, there came out to them Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder.
verses.18:19: Then the Rabshakeh said to them, "Say now to Hezekiah, thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?
verses.18:20: You say—mere words of the lips—that you have counsel and might for war. Now in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
verses.18:21: Now behold, you are trusting on the staff of this crushed reed, on Egypt, on which if a man leans, it will enter his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
verses.18:22: But if you say to me, 'We trust in the LORD our God,' is it not He whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has removed, and has said to Judah and to Jerusalem, 'You shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem'?
verses.18:23: Now therefore, come, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders upon them.
verses.18:24: How then can you turn back a single governor of the least of my master's servants, and put your trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
verses.18:25: Have I now come up without the LORD against this place to destroy it? The LORD said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
verses.18:26: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; and do not speak with us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people who are on the wall."
verses.18:27: But the Rabshakeh said to them, "Has my master sent me to your master and to you to speak these words, and not to the men who sit upon the wall, to eat their own waste and to drink the water of their feet with you?"
verses.18:28: Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out with a loud voice in the language of Judah, and spoke, saying, "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
verses.18:29: Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you from his hand;
verses.18:30: nor let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, 'The LORD will surely deliver us, and this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'
verses.18:31: Do not listen to Hezekiah; for thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me and come out to me, and every one of you shall eat from his own vine and every one from his own fig tree, and every one of you shall drink the waters of his own cistern,
verses.18:32: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, that you may live and not die. And do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you, saying, 'The LORD will deliver us.'
verses.18:33: Has any of the gods of the nations at all delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
verses.18:34: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they indeed delivered Samaria from my hand?
verses.18:35: Who among all the gods of the lands have delivered their land from my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
verses.18:36: But the people remained silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."
verses.18:37: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.
verses.19:1: And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his garments, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
verses.19:2: Then he sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
verses.19:3: And they said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: 'This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of scorn; for the children have come to the point of birth, yet there is no strength to give birth.
verses.19:4: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to reproach the living God, and will rebuke the words which the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left.'"
verses.19:5: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.19:6: And Isaiah said to them, "Thus you shall say to your master: 'Thus says the LORD: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the attendants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
verses.19:7: Behold, I will put a spirit in him, and he shall hear a rumor and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.'"
verses.19:8: Then the Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
verses.19:9: And when he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, "Behold, he has come out to fight against you," he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying,
verses.19:10: "Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying: 'Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, "Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."
verses.19:11: Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands by utterly destroying them; and shall you be delivered?
verses.19:12: Have the gods of the nations delivered those whom my fathers destroyed—Gozan and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were in Telassar?
verses.19:13: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivvah?'"
verses.19:14: And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it; and he went up to the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah spread it out before the LORD.
verses.19:15: Then Hezekiah prayed before the LORD and said, "O LORD, the God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You are God, You alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; You have made heaven and earth.
verses.19:16: Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to reproach the living God.
verses.19:17: Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands,
verses.19:18: and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were not gods, but the work of men's hands—wood and stone—and so they destroyed them.
verses.19:19: Now therefore, O LORD our God, save us, I pray, from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You, O LORD, are God alone."
verses.19:20: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'What you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard.'
verses.19:21: This is the word which the LORD has spoken concerning him: 'The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and mocked you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head behind you.
verses.19:22: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? And against whom have you raised your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!
verses.19:23: By your messengers you have reproached the Lord, and you have said, "With the multitude of my chariots I have ascended the height of the mountains, the remotest parts of Lebanon; I will cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees; and I will enter its farthest lodging place, the forest of its fruitful land.
verses.19:24: I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters, and with the soles of my feet I will dry up all the streams of Egypt."
verses.19:25: Have you not heard that long ago I made it, from ancient days I formed it? Now I have brought it to pass, that you should lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.
verses.19:26: Therefore their inhabitants were of little strength; they were dismayed and put to shame. They became like the grass of the field and the green herb, like grass on the housetops, blighted before it is grown.
verses.19:27: But I know your sitting down, your going out and your coming in, and your raging against Me.
verses.19:28: Because of your raging against Me, and because your arrogance has come up into My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.'
verses.19:29: And this shall be the sign for you: You shall eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from the same; and in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
verses.19:30: And the escaped remnant of the house of Judah that remains shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
verses.19:31: For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and those who escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts shall perform this.
verses.19:32: Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: 'He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast up a siege mound against it.
verses.19:33: By the way that he came, by the same he shall return; and he shall not come into this city, declares the LORD.
verses.19:34: For I will defend this city to save it, for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.'"
verses.19:35: And it came to pass on that night that the angel of the LORD went out and struck down in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred and eighty-five thousand; and when men rose early in the morning, behold, all of them were dead bodies.
verses.19:36: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed and went away, returned home, and dwelt in Nineveh.
verses.19:37: And it came to pass, as he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. Then Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.
verses.20:1: In those days Hezekiah was sick to the point of death. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Set your house in order, for you shall die and not live.'"
verses.20:2: Then he turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying,
verses.20:3: "O LORD, remember now, I pray, how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your sight." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
verses.20:4: And it happened, before Isaiah had gone out from the middle court, that the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.20:5: "Return and speak to Hezekiah the leader of My people: 'Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I will heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of the LORD.
verses.20:6: And I will add to your days fifteen years. I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will defend this city for My own sake, and for the sake of My servant David.'"
verses.20:7: Then Isaiah said, "Take a cake of figs." So they took it and laid it on the boil, and he recovered.
verses.20:8: And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What shall be the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I shall go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"
verses.20:9: Then Isaiah said, "This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do the thing which He has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or turn back ten steps?"
verses.20:10: And Hezekiah answered, "It is an easy thing for the shadow to go down ten steps; no, rather let the shadow turn backward ten steps."
verses.20:11: So Isaiah the prophet cried out to the LORD, and He brought the shadow back ten steps, along the steps by which it had gone down on the stairway of Ahaz.
verses.20:12: At that time Berodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.
verses.20:13: And Hezekiah listened to them, and showed them all his treasure house—the silver and the gold, the spices and the precious oil, and his armory, and all that was found among his treasuries. There was nothing in his house or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.
verses.20:14: Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and from where did they come to you?" And Hezekiah said, "They came from a far country, from Babylon."
verses.20:15: And he said, "What have they seen in your house?" So Hezekiah answered, "They have seen all that is in my house; there is nothing among my treasuries that I have not shown them."
verses.20:16: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD:
verses.20:17: 'Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be carried to Babylon; nothing shall be left, says the LORD.
verses.20:18: And some of your sons who shall come forth from you, whom you shall father, shall be taken away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.'"
verses.20:19: So Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "Good is the word of the LORD which you have spoken." For he said, "Is it not good, if peace and truth shall be in my days?"
verses.20:20: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.20:21: So Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.
verses.21:2: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the children of Israel.
verses.21:3: For he rebuilt the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; he raised up altars for Baal and made an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel had done; and he bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.21:4: He also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem I will place My name."
verses.21:5: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.
verses.21:6: Also he made his son pass through the fire, practiced soothsaying, used divination, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He multiplied evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.21:7: He even set the carved image of Asherah that he had made in the house of which the LORD had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will place My name forever;
verses.21:8: and I will not again make the foot of Israel wander from the land which I gave to their fathers—only if they are careful to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that My servant Moses commanded them."
verses.21:9: Yet they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the children of Israel.
verses.21:10: And the LORD spoke by His servants the prophets, saying,
verses.21:11: "Because Manasseh king of Judah has committed these abominations—having done more wickedly than all that the Amorites did who were before him—and has also caused Judah to sin with his idols,
verses.21:12: therefore thus says the LORD God of Israel: 'Behold, I am bringing such calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah that whoever hears of it, both his ears shall tingle.
verses.21:13: And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab; I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.
verses.21:14: So I will forsake the remnant of My inheritance and deliver them into the hand of their enemies, and they shall become prey and plunder to all their enemies,
verses.21:15: because they have done what was evil in My sight and have continually provoked Me to anger from the day their fathers came out of Egypt, even to this day.'"
verses.21:16: Moreover Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another, besides his sin by which he made Judah sin, in doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.21:17: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all that he did, and the sin that he committed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:18: So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza. Then Amon his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:19: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
verses.21:20: And he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done.
verses.21:21: So he walked in all the way that his father had walked, and he served the idols that his father had served and bowed down to them.
verses.21:22: He forsook the LORD God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.
verses.21:23: Then the servants of Amon conspired against him, and put the king to death in his own house.
verses.21:24: But the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon. Then the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.21:25: Now the rest of the acts of Amon which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:26: And he was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. Then Josiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:1: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
verses.22:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in all the way of his father David; he did not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
verses.22:3: Now it came to pass, in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, that the king sent Shaphan the scribe, the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, to the house of the LORD, saying,
verses.22:4: "Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, that he may sum up the money which has been brought into the house of the LORD, which the keepers of the threshold have collected from the people.
verses.22:5: And let them deliver it into the hand of the workmen who have the oversight of the house of the LORD; and let them give it to the workmen who are in the house of the LORD, to repair the breaches of the house,
verses.22:6: to the carpenters and builders and masons, and to buy timber and hewn stone to repair the house.
verses.22:7: However, no accounting shall be made with them for the money delivered into their hand, because they deal faithfully."
verses.22:8: Then Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
verses.22:9: So Shaphan the scribe came to the king, brought word back to the king, and said, "Your servants have poured out the money that was found in the house, and have delivered it into the hand of the workmen who have the oversight of the house of the LORD."
verses.22:10: Then Shaphan the scribe informed the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read it before the king.
verses.22:11: Now it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, that he tore his garments.
verses.22:12: Then the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Achbor the son of Michaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah a servant of the king, saying,
verses.22:13: "Go, inquire of the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not heeded the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us."
verses.22:14: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe—now she dwelt in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter—and they spoke with her.
verses.22:15: Then she said to them, "Thus says the LORD God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
verses.22:16: 'Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am bringing calamity upon this place and upon its inhabitants, even all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read,
verses.22:17: because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods, so as to provoke Me to anger with all the work of their hands; therefore My wrath shall be kindled against this place, and it shall not be quenched.'
verses.22:18: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus you shall say to him: 'Thus says the LORD God of Israel: As for the words which you have heard,
verses.22:19: because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before Me, I also have heard, declares the LORD.
verses.22:20: Therefore, behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace; and your eyes shall not see all the calamity which I am bringing upon this place.'" So they brought word back to the king.
verses.23:1: Then the king sent word, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.23:2: And the king went up to the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets, and all the people, from the least to the greatest; and he read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant which had been found in the house of the LORD.
verses.23:3: Then the king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and to keep His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to establish the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people took their stand in the covenant.
verses.23:4: And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out of the temple of the LORD all the vessels that had been made for Baal, and for Asherah, and for all the host of heaven; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried their ashes to Bethel.
verses.23:5: And he deposed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the cities of Judah and in the places all around Jerusalem, and also those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.
verses.23:6: And he brought out the Asherah from the house of the LORD, outside Jerusalem to the Brook Kidron, and burned it at the Brook Kidron and ground it to dust, and cast its dust upon the graves of the common people.
verses.23:7: And he tore down the houses of the male cult prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women wove hangings for Asherah.
verses.23:8: And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba; and he broke down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the Gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man's left at the gate of the city.
verses.23:9: Nevertheless, the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brethren.
verses.23:10: And he defiled Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
verses.23:11: And he removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, at the entrance to the house of the LORD, by the chamber of Nathan-Melech the officer, which was in the precincts; and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.
verses.23:12: And the altars that were on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD, the king broke down and crushed them there, and cast their dust into the Brook Kidron.
verses.23:13: Then the king defiled the high places that were before Jerusalem, on the south of the Mount of Corruption, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the detestable thing of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon.
verses.23:14: And he shattered the sacred pillars and cut down the Asherah poles, and filled their places with the bones of men.
verses.23:15: Moreover, the altar that was at Bethel, and the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, had made—both that altar and the high place he broke down; and he burned the high place, ground it to dust, and burned the Asherah.
verses.23:16: And as Josiah turned, he saw the tombs that were there on the mountain. And he sent and took the bones out of the tombs and burned them on the altar, and defiled it according to the word of the LORD which the man of God had proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.
verses.23:17: Then he said, "What monument is this that I see?" And the men of the city said to him, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things which you have done against the altar of Bethel."
verses.23:18: And he said, "Let him alone; let no man disturb his bones." So they left his bones undisturbed, together with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
verses.23:19: Josiah also removed all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke anger; and he did to them according to all the deeds that he had done in Bethel.
verses.23:20: And he slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars, and burned the bones of men upon them; then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.23:21: Then the king commanded all the people, saying, "Keep the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant."
verses.23:22: For no such Passover had been kept since the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
verses.23:23: But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, this Passover was kept to the LORD in Jerusalem.
verses.23:24: Moreover, Josiah put away the mediums and the spiritists, and the household idols and the idols, and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, in order that he might establish the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.
verses.23:25: And before him there was no king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the Law of Moses; nor after him did any arise like him.
verses.23:26: Nevertheless, the LORD did not turn from the fierceness of His great wrath, with which His anger burned against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.
verses.23:27: And the LORD said, "I will also remove Judah from My sight, as I have removed Israel, and I will reject this city which I have chosen—Jerusalem—and the house of which I said, 'My name shall be there.'"
verses.23:28: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.23:29: In his days Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the River Euphrates; and King Josiah went out to meet him, and he slew him at Megiddo as soon as he saw him.
verses.23:30: And his servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
verses.23:31: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.23:32: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.23:33: Now Pharaoh Necho put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and he laid a tribute upon the land of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
verses.23:34: And Pharaoh Necho made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. And he took Jehoahaz away; and he came to Egypt and died there.
verses.23:35: So Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; but he taxed the land to give the money according to the command of Pharaoh; he exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, from each man according to his assessment, to give to Pharaoh Necho.
verses.23:36: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Zebudah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
verses.23:37: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.24:1: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.
verses.24:2: And the LORD sent against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, and bands of Syrians, and bands of Moabites, and bands of the children of Ammon; and He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD which He had spoken by the hand of His servants the prophets.
verses.24:3: Surely at the command of the LORD this came upon Judah, to remove them from His sight, because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
verses.24:4: and also because of the innocent blood that he had shed, for he had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; and the LORD was not willing to pardon.
verses.24:5: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.24:6: So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
verses.24:7: And the king of Egypt did not come out of his land anymore, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Brook of Egypt to the River Euphrates.
verses.24:8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
verses.24:9: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.
verses.24:10: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
verses.24:11: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, while his servants were besieging it.
verses.24:12: Then Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants, and his princes, and his officers; and the king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.24:13: And he carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house, and he cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had spoken.
verses.24:14: And he carried away into exile all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valor—ten thousand captives—and all the craftsmen and the smiths; none remained, except the poorest of the people of the land.
verses.24:15: And he carried Jehoiachin away into exile to Babylon; and the king's mother, and the king's wives, and his officers, and the leading men of the land, he led into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.24:16: And all the men of valor, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths, one thousand, all of them mighty men fit for war—these the king of Babylon brought into exile to Babylon.
verses.24:17: Then the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, his uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
verses.24:18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.24:19: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.24:20: For because of the anger of the LORD it came to pass in Jerusalem and in Judah, until He had cast them out from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.25:1: Now it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and encamped against it; and they built a siege wall against it all around.
verses.25:2: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.25:3: On the ninth day of the month, the famine grew severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.25:4: Then the city was breached, and all the men of war fled by night by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were around the city; and he went by the way of the Arabah.
verses.25:5: Yet the forces of the Chaldeans pursued after the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army dispersed from him.
verses.25:6: So they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they pronounced judgment upon him.
verses.25:7: And they slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah, bound him with bronze fetters, and brought him to Babylon.
verses.25:8: Now in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.25:9: And he burned the house of the LORD and the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem; even every great house he burned with fire.
verses.25:11: And the rest of the people who remained in the city, and the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, along with the rest of the multitude, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away into exile.
verses.25:12: But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and plowmen.
verses.25:13: Moreover, the Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of bronze that were in the house of the LORD, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, and carried their bronze to Babylon.
verses.25:14: They also took the pots, the shovels, the trimmers, the ladles, and all the vessels of bronze with which they ministered.
verses.25:15: And the firepans and the basins—what was of gold as gold, and what was of silver as silver—the captain of the guard took away.
verses.25:16: As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the stands which Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these vessels could not be weighed.
verses.25:17: The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and upon it was a capital of bronze; and the height of the capital was three cubits, with latticework and pomegranates upon the capital all around, all of bronze. And the second pillar had the same, with latticework.
verses.25:18: Then the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.
verses.25:19: And from the city he took one officer who was appointed over the men of war, and five men of those who saw the king's face who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
verses.25:20: So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.25:21: And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away into exile from its own land.
verses.25:22: Now over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.
verses.25:23: And when all the commanders of the forces, they and the men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, Johanan the son of Kareah, Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
verses.25:24: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you."
verses.25:25: Now it came to pass in the seventh month that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal seed, came, and ten men with him, and they struck down Gedaliah so that he died, along with the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
verses.25:26: Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, and the commanders of the forces arose and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.
verses.25:27: Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison.
verses.25:28: And he spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.25:29: So he changed his prison garments, and ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.
verses.25:30: And as for his allowance, a continual allowance was given to him from the king, a portion for each day, all the days of his life.

notes.1:2: Baal-Zebub means "lord of flies," widely understood as a deliberate Hebrew polemical wordplay on Baal-Zebul, "Baal the Prince."
notes.1:8: "A hairy man" renders the Hebrew idiom meaning literally "a man, master of hair," referring either to bodily hair or to a coarse garment of animal hair worn by prophets.
notes.1:17: This synchronism with the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat reflects a period of co-regency between Jehoshaphat and his son Jehoram in Judah.
notes.2:9: "A double portion" reflects the firstborn's legal inheritance share (Deuteronomy 21:17), expressing Elisha's request to succeed Elijah as his chief prophetic heir.
notes.2:16: Ketiv/Qere: the ketiv writes an alternative plural spelling of "the valleys," while the qere reads the standard vocalized plural form translated here.
notes.2:19: "Barren" renders a Hebrew participle meaning literally "bereaving" or "causing miscarriage and unfruitfulness," repeated in verse 21.
notes.3:4: Mesha king of Moab is also attested in the ninth-century BC Mesha Stele, which records his rebellion against the house of Omri from a Moabite perspective.
notes.3:16: "Full of trenches" renders the Hebrew repetition "trenches, trenches," an idiom denoting many water-catching pits dug across the dry valley floor.
notes.3:24: Ketiv/Qere: the translation follows the qere, "and they struck into it," referring to the land of Moab; the ketiv writes "and they entered into it."
notes.3:27: "Great wrath against Israel" translates a terse Hebrew phrase understood either as fierce Moabite fury provoked by the king's sacrifice or as divine displeasure leading to Israel's withdrawal.
notes.4:2: Here and in 4:3, 4:7, 4:16, and 4:23, the ketiv preserves archaic second-person feminine singular forms, while the qere provides the standard Masoretic forms.
notes.4:5: Qere reads a feminine participle form meaning pouring out; ketiv preserves a variant spelling of the same verb with identical sense.
notes.4:16: Literally at this appointed season, as the time of life, a Hebrew idiom denoting the corresponding time in the coming year.
notes.4:42: The Hebrew noun rendered sack occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and refers to a pouch or bag for carrying grain.
notes.5:1: Aram is the Hebrew name for the ancient kingdom of Syria, whose capital was Damascus.
notes.5:12: Qere reads Amanah, the chief river flowing through Damascus; ketiv reads Abanah.
notes.5:18: In the second petition, the ketiv includes the Hebrew entreaty particle na (please), which is not read in the qere.
notes.5:25: Qere reads the full interrogative form meaning from where; ketiv writes a defective spelling with the same meaning.
notes.6:25: The Masoretic Qere reads a euphemistic form for the Ketiv term meaning "dove's dung"; a kab was a dry measure of roughly one to two quarts.
notes.6:27: The Hebrew idiom literally uses a negative jussive that functions conditionally here, "If the LORD does not help you."
notes.6:33: The Masoretic Text has "the messenger" arriving and speaking in the king's name, while the king follows immediately behind him (compare 6:32 and 7:17).
notes.7:1: A seah was a dry measure equal to roughly seven to eight quarts.
notes.7:12: The Qere reads the standard contracted form "in the field," whereas the Ketiv retains the uncontracted definite article.
notes.7:13: The Qere omits the definite article found in the Ketiv before the construct noun "multitude," and the translation preserves the Masoretic Text's repeated comparison.
notes.7:15: The Qere vocalizes "in their haste" as a Qal infinitive rather than the Ketiv's Niphal form, with the same meaning.
notes.8:1: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads the archaic feminine pronoun 'atti', while the Masoretic Qere reads standard 'att' ("you").
notes.8:10: Ketiv/Qere: the Masoretic Qere reads 'lo' ("to him"), yielding "say to him, 'You shall surely recover,'" whereas the Ketiv reads 'lo' ("not"), yielding "say, 'You shall certainly not recover.'"
notes.8:16: Throughout chapters 8 and 9, the Hebrew text alternates between the short form Joram and the full form Jehoram for both the king of Israel and the king of Judah; this translation mirrors the spelling of each occurrence.
notes.8:26: Hebrew 'bat' ("daughter") here denotes a granddaughter or female descendant of Omri's royal line; Athaliah was the daughter of Ahab (cf. 8:18).
notes.9:8: "Every male" renders a blunt Hebrew idiom, literally "him who urinates against a wall," denoting all male members of the household.
notes.9:15: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv writes the contracted infinitive 'lagid', while the Qere reads the standard form 'lehaggid' ("to report").
notes.9:33: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads 'shamtuhu', while the Masoretic Qere reads the feminine-object imperative 'shimtuha' ("Throw her down!").
notes.9:37: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv preserves the archaic third-person feminine singular perfect 'wehayat', while the Qere reads standard 'wehayetah' ("and it shall be").
notes.10:1: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "rulers of Jezreel" (though the letters are sent to Samaria) and literally "the guardians, Ahab," referring to those who reared Ahab's sons.
notes.10:12: Beth Eked of the Shepherds literally means "the house of binding of the shepherds," likely a shearing station along the road from Jezreel to Samaria.
notes.10:25: "Inner sanctuary" translates a Hebrew word normally meaning "city" or "citadel," used here for the innermost chamber of Baal's temple.
notes.10:27: The Qere (read form) is a euphemism meaning "a latrine" (literally "places of going out"), replacing the coarser Ketiv (written form) meaning "a dung-house."
notes.11:1: The Qere (read form) omits the initial conjunction on "saw," whereas the Ketiv (written form) includes it.
notes.11:2: The Qere (read form) reads a standard passive participle ("who were being put to death"), clarifying the unusual consonantal form in the Ketiv.
notes.11:4: Here and in verses 9, 10, and 15, the Qere (read form) standardizes the spelling of "hundreds" from an older Ketiv spelling; the Carites were an elite corps of royal bodyguards.
notes.11:6: "As a defense" renders a rare Hebrew term occurring only here, understood to mean guarding against intrusion or keeping watch in alternating shifts.
notes.11:20: The Qere (read form) supplies the definite article in "the king's house," where the Ketiv (written form) omits it.
notes.12:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification, chapter 12 begins with this verse, which appears as 11:21 in many English Bibles; consequently, the remaining verses of chapter 12 are numbered one higher than in those versions.
notes.12:5: Hebrew kesef over, literally money of one passing over, refers either to the census assessment paid by each man who passed the numbering (Exodus 30:13) or to current silver.
notes.12:10: The Hebrew Qere reads miyyamin (on the right side), whereas the Ketiv reads beyamin (at the right side); the translation follows the Qere.
notes.12:12: Two Ketiv/Qere variants occur here: the Qere reads yedei (hands) against Ketiv yad (hand), and hammufqadim (who had the oversight, Hophal participle) against Ketiv happequdim; the translation follows the Qere in both places.
notes.12:18: The Hebrew name Aram is rendered traditionally as Syria throughout chapters 12 and 13.
notes.13:1: The Masoretic text alternates between the fuller spelling Jehoash and the shorter spelling Joash for both the king of Judah and the king of Israel.
notes.13:6: The Asherah was a sacred wooden pole or cultic image associated with the Canaanite goddess Asherah, erected in Samaria during the reign of Ahab (1 Kings 16:33).
notes.13:17: Literally an arrow of deliverance belonging to the LORD, signifying a victory granted by the LORD over Syria (Aram).
notes.13:20: Literally at the coming of the year, referring to the spring season when military campaigns and raids resumed.
notes.14:2: The Qere (read text) gives the name Jehoaddan, whereas the Ketiv (written text) reads Jehoaddin.
notes.14:6: The Qere reads the passive form "shall be put to death," matching the preceding clauses (cf. Deuteronomy 24:16), whereas the Ketiv reads the active "shall die."
notes.14:7: The Ketiv and Qere differ only on the definite article attached to "Salt" in "the Valley of Salt," with no change in meaning.
notes.14:13: The Qere reads the singular verb "he came," referring to Jehoash, whereas the Ketiv reads the plural "they came."
notes.14:28: The Hebrew reads literally "restored Damascus and Hamath for Judah in Israel," pointing to northern territories once subject to the united kingdom of David and Solomon.
notes.15:5: "A separate house" translates the Hebrew phrase for a secluded residence set apart for the king because of his leprosy.
notes.15:10: "Before the people" translates the Masoretic Hebrew phrase indicating that Shallum assassinated Zechariah publicly in the presence of the populace.
notes.15:13: Azariah king of Judah is also called Uzziah in this verse and in verses 30, 32, and 34.
notes.15:25: The Qere supplies the definite article in "the king's house," whereas the Ketiv omits it; the phrase "along with Argob and Arieh" may refer either to officials slain beside Pekahiah or to fellow conspirators with Pekah.
notes.16:6: Translates the Masoretic qere "and the Edomites"; the ketiv reads "and the Syrians" (Arameans), reflecting the visual similarity of the Hebrew letters dalet and resh.
notes.16:15: Translates the qere "commanded" without the redundant object suffix of the ketiv ("commanded him"). The Hebrew verb translated "to inquire by" can denote seeking oracular guidance or priestly inspection.
notes.16:18: Translates the qere musak ("covered portico" or "canopy"); the ketiv misak is an orthographic variant with the same sense.
notes.17:13: Translates the Masoretic qere "all the prophets, every seer"; the ketiv reads "all His prophets" (or "every prophet of His").
notes.17:21: Translates the Masoretic qere "drove away" (from the root meaning to thrust or entice away); the ketiv preserves an unusual orthographic form with the same sense.
notes.17:27: The Hebrew text uses plural verbs ("let them go and dwell there") before returning to the singular ("let him teach them"), encompassing the priest together with those accompanying him.
notes.17:31: Translates the Masoretic qere "the gods of Sepharvaim," correcting the defective spellings in the ketiv.
notes.18:4: Nehushtan is a Hebrew wordplay connecting the terms for bronze and serpent, referring to the bronze serpent made by Moses in the wilderness.
notes.18:17: The Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Rabshakeh are Assyrian court and military titles designating high-ranking royal officials rather than personal names.
notes.18:27: Their own waste and the water of their feet follow the Masoretic Qere, which substitutes polite euphemisms for the blunter Ketiv terms meaning dung and urine.
notes.18:29: From his hand follows the Masoretic Hebrew, referring to the king of Assyria in the third person.
notes.18:31: Make peace with me is literally make a blessing with me, a Hebrew idiom for coming to terms of peace and submission.
notes.19:23: The Qere reads berov ("with the multitude of"), translated here, whereas the Ketiv reads berekhev ("with the chariotry of"). The phrase ye'orei matsor ("streams of Egypt") uses a poetic name for Egypt and may alternatively be rendered "streams of besieged places."
notes.19:31: The word tseva'ot ("of hosts") is a Masoretic Qere without Ketiv, read in the synagogue tradition though absent from the written consonantal text (compare Isaiah 37:32).
notes.19:37: The word banav ("his sons") is a Masoretic Qere without Ketiv, read in tradition and attested in the parallel account of Isaiah 37:38.
notes.20:4: The Qere reads chatser ("court," referring to the middle court of the palace complex), translated here, whereas the Ketiv reads ha'ir ("the city").
notes.20:9: The Hebrew ma'alot literally means "steps" and refers to the graduated stairway of Ahaz (verse 11), whose shadow served as a timekeeping dial.
notes.20:12: The Hebrew text here spells the Babylonian king's name Berodach-baladan, corresponding to Merodach-baladan in Isaiah 39:1.
notes.20:18: The Qere reads the plural yiqqachu ("they shall take," rendered passively "shall be taken"), whereas the Ketiv reads the singular yiqqach ("he/one shall take").
notes.21:12: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere (שֹׁמְעָהּ, "whoever hears of it"), with the feminine suffix referring back to the coming calamity; the Ketiv reads שמעיו.
notes.21:13: The "measuring line of Samaria" and "plummet of the house of Ahab" are builder's tools inverted as metaphors of judgment, signifying that Jerusalem will be measured out for the same ruin that befell the northern kingdom.
notes.21:16: "From one end to another" renders the vivid Hebrew idiom "mouth to mouth," denoting that the city was filled completely from border to border.
notes.22:5: The translation follows both Masoretic Qere readings: "and let them deliver it" (Qere וְיִתְּנוּהוּ; Ketiv ויתנה) and "of the house" (Qere בֵּית; Ketiv בבית, "in the house").
notes.22:9: "Poured out" translates a Hebrew verb (הִתִּיכוּ) meaning to empty out or melt down, describing the emptying of the collected silver from the temple chests for distribution to the overseers.
notes.22:14: "The Second Quarter" (Hebrew ha-Mishneh) refers to the newer western district of Jerusalem developed as the city expanded beyond its original walls.
notes.23:7: Hebrew battim, literally houses, here denotes woven hangings or tent-shrines made for Asherah.
notes.23:10: Following the Masoretic Qere ben-Hinnom (Son of Hinnom); the Ketiv reads the plural bney-Hinnom (sons of Hinnom).
notes.23:12: The Hebrew verb is vocalized as a form of ruts (run), though in this context it is widely understood as a form of ratsats (crush or pulverize), corresponding to the following mention of their dust.
notes.23:33: Following the Qere mimmelokh (from reigning); the Ketiv reads bemelokh (while reigning).
notes.23:36: Following the Qere Zebudah; the Ketiv spells the name Zebidah.
notes.24:10: Following the Qere plural verb alu (came up), agreeing with the plural subject servants; the Ketiv reads the singular alah.
notes.24:14: Following the Qere construct numeral aseret (ten) before alafim (thousands); the Ketiv writes the absolute form asarah.
notes.24:15: Following the Qere eyley ha-arets (the leading or mighty men of the land); the Ketiv is an orthographic variant with waw.
notes.24:18: Following the Qere Hamutal, matching the spelling in 23:31; the Ketiv spells the name Hamital.
notes.25:4: The Hebrew text omits the verb before "by night," which is supplied as "fled" from the context, and shifts to a singular verb ("he went") referring to King Zedekiah.
notes.25:6: Literally "they spoke judgment with him," a Hebrew idiom for holding a judicial hearing and pronouncing formal sentence.
notes.25:17: The Masoretic qere reads the plural "cubits," whereas the written ketiv has the singular "cubit."
notes.25:27: "Lifted up the head" is a Hebrew idiom meaning to restore a prisoner to favor and grant release.
